question: At what ages is the onset of secondary sexual characteristics considered to indicate PRECOCIOUS puberty, by current definitions?

answers.text: Before 9 years in girls and before 10 years in boys

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: These thresholds are incorrect. The standard cut-offs are younger than those stated here — recalling the correct ages is a foundational clinical skill for paediatric endocrine referral.

answers.text: Before 8 years in girls and before 9 years in boys

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Precocious puberty is defined as onset of puberty before 8 years in girls (thelarche is the first sign) and before 9 years in boys (testicular enlargement >4 mL). These thresholds trigger investigation and referral.

answers.text: Before 10 years in girls and before 11 years in boys

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: These are approximately the mean ages of onset of normal puberty, not the precocious-puberty cut-offs. Precocious puberty thresholds are set ~2 SD below the mean: <8 yr girls, <9 yr boys.

answers.text: Before 8 years in girls and before 8 years in boys

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The threshold for boys is 9 years, not 8 years. Girls: <8 yr; boys: <9 yr — there is a 1-year difference between the sexes.

overallFeedback.feedback: The fixed thresholds: precocious puberty = <8 yr (girls) and <9 yr (boys). These numbers are tested in exams and are the clinical trigger for referral — learn them precisely.
Excellent. Commit these: precocious puberty = <8 yr in girls, <9 yr in boys. Delayed puberty = no development by 13 yr in girls, no testicular enlargement by 14 yr in boys.
